outcome: The unconditional decidability of the theory of the real exponential field remains open; the positive answer is still known only modulo Schanuel's conjecture (Macintyre–Wilkie 1996), and no result in the window changes this.
summary: Tarski's exponential function problem — whether the first-order theory of (ℝ; +, ·, exp, <, 0, 1) is decidable — remains open in its unconditional form as of September 2026. The only positive result is still Macintyre and Wilkie's 1996 conditional theorem (decidability follows from Schanuel's conjecture), which predates the frozen revision by decades and is not itself a change. Several papers touch adjacent territory in the window but none of them are a case of, nor change, the stated problem under the §3.1 scope rule: (1) Gallego-Hernández and Mansutti, 'On the Existential Theory of the Reals Enriched with Integer Powers of a Computable Number' (arXiv:2502.02220, STACS 2025), studies a structurally different, much weaker language — ℝ with a unary predicate for integer powers of one fixed computable real ξ, restricted to the existential fragment — and explicitly frames this as a tame variant that avoids Schanuel's conjecture rather than as progress on the full exponential theory; it is a related problem, not a restriction of Tarski's stated question, since the exponential function itself is absent from the language. (2) Berarducci and Gallinaro, 'On the elementary theory of the real exponential field' (arXiv:2603.08365, submitted March 2026, revised June 2026), is the most substantive item found: assuming Schanuel's conjecture, they give a new axiomatization (definably complete exponential fields with exp′=exp) of the complete theory T_exp, from which the Macintyre–Wilkie decidability result again follows — still conditional, not a new unconditional result on the problem itself. They do prove one piece unconditionally (model completeness of the restricted axioms for exp on (−1,1)), but this is a technical lemma feeding a conditional axiomatization, not a change to what a careful reader would write in Tarski's own bullet: the theory's decidability is still open unconditionally. Schanuel's conjecture itself, on which the whole conditional edifice rests, also remains unproven; recent work found (Waldschmidt's note on elliptic/quasi-elliptic analogues, and 'Schanuel Property for Elliptic and Quasi-Elliptic Functions', arXiv:2504.14041) proves measure-one or analogue versions for different structures, not the real Schanuel conjecture needed here. I also checked proofatlas.ai's page for Schanuel's Conjecture, an AI-assisted 'collaboration' research-tracking platform; it explicitly states 'Revision v6 explicitly reports no proof' and documents open routes and obstacles rather than any result, and notes no AI-assisted proof attempt on this conjecture. No source anywhere in this search attributes any part of the (non-)progress to an AI system: the STACS and Berarducci–Gallinaro papers are traditional pure model theory/logic papers with no acknowledgement of AI tools, and no lab announcement, AI-solved-problem list, or AI mathematics report mentions this problem. Triage's verdict (`none`) and its account of the 2502.02220 paper are correct; I confirm and add the 2603.08365 paper as a second, more directly relevant near-miss the triage did not surface, though it too does not change the status.
competing_reading: One could argue Berarducci–Gallinaro's unconditional model-completeness result for the restricted (−1,1) exponential axioms is 'progress' worth a status of `progress` rather than `open`, since it is a genuine new unconditional theorem in the immediate technical vicinity of the problem. I read it as not in scope: it is a lemma about an axiom system for a bounded restriction of the function, used only to rebuild the conditional decidability argument, and it does not itself decide, or narrow the undecided status of, any fragment of Th(ℝ, exp). It does not remove any case from the stated existential/universal decision question the way a settled special case would. If a downstream reader treats any unconditional structural theorem adjacent to T_exp as movement on the bullet, this should be `progress` with `ai_role` `none` and `resolution_direction` null; the outcome and AI conclusions would be unchanged either way.
what_would_settle_it: An unconditional decision procedure (or unconditional undecidability proof) for Th(ℝ, +, ·, exp, <), or an unconditional proof/disproof of the real Schanuel conjecture, would settle the classification question definitively — as would an explicit statement from a subsequent paper that Berarducci–Gallinaro's lemma decides some previously-undecided fragment of the theory.
